editorial:
Imagine a world where the guy hired to catch the bad guy is just as mean as the criminal. That is exactly what you get with Harry Clegg. He is an ex-cop who does not play by the rules, and he is brought in to hunt down a dangerous woman who has been killing people. The vibe is gritty and dark, making you feel like you are walking through the rainy, gray streets of a city where nobody can be trusted. It feels less like a polished police show and more like a raw, dirty street fight, which keeps you on edge from the start.

What really works here is how the tension builds as Clegg gets closer to his target. The acting is solid, though the pacing slows down in a few spots. You will love it if you enjoy old-school crime stories where the hero is actually a bit of a jerk. If you can find a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, that is the way to go for the best picture. Otherwise, look for it while renting on Apple TV to see those grainy 70s visuals in the best quality possible.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with a tense showdown where Clegg finally catches up to the killer. After a long game of cat and mouse, the truth comes out about why she was killing. There is a final twist where the lines between the hunter and the hunted blur. Clegg uses his dirty tactics one last time to finish the job, ensuring the murderer is stopped once and for all in a cold, unsentimental way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school detective stories and anti-hero leads.
